{{Short description|Theorem in group theory}}
{{one source |date=May 2024}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''B-theorem''' is a result in [[Group theory#Finite group theory|finite group theory]] formerly known as the '''B-conjecture'''.

The [[theorem]] states that if <math>C</math> is the [[centralizer and normalizer|centralizer]] of an [[involution (mathematics)|involution]] of a [[finite group]], then every component of <math>C/O(C)</math> is the image of a component of <math>C</math>.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Gorenstein|first1=Daniel|title=The Classification of finite simple groups|date=1983|publisher=Plenum Press|location=New York|isbn=978-0-306-41305-6|page=7}}</ref>
